newsitem.title: USA: Bond dealers testify against de minimis repeal.
newsitem.headline: Bond dealers testify against de minimis repeal.

text.p: Bond dealers were expected to urge Wednesday a key U.S. House panel to reject a Clinton Administration proposal to repeal the two-percent "de minimis" rule on corporate holdings of tax-exempt bonds, according to a statement released a by a bond trade group.

Arthur Hyde, chairman of the corporate bond division of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, was expected to tell the House Ways and Means Committee that Clinton's plan "would make it more expensive for state and local governments to finance vital public services," according to the statement.
Currently, the Internal Revenue Service does not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total no more than two percent.
Clinton in his proposed fiscal 1998 federal budget called for repeal of the "de minimis" standard in an effort to close what he called corporate loopholes.
But unlike a repeal bill he unsuccessfully pushed last year, the latest measure would not be retractive. The effective date would be the date of first congressional committee approval of the measure.
Hyde is planning to tell the House panel on Wednesday that PSA is pleased with Clinton's new effective date, but remains "steadfastly opposed" to the basic repeal plan.
"The administration's proposal would effectively discourage virtually all corporate investment in the municipal market," Hyde is expected to tell the panel, according to the PSA statement.
It not only would raise the cost of short-term borrowing for localities, but it would make short-term municipal rates more volatile compared to taxable rates, Hyde is expected to say.

Hyde is planning to say that the administration's plan implies that corporations have "deliberately engaged in arbitrage practices by borrowing in the short-term market and investing in tax-exempt obligataions."

He is also planning to say there is no evidence that is happening, accoirding to the PSA statement. "Holdings of municipal bonds have averaged only 0.47 percent of the financial assets and 0.15 percent of the total assets of non-financial corporations since 1987."
